scripts._selftest_coverage_law: ISSUE #75 (2026-08-04) · MEMBERSHIP MOVED TO FILES by unit mhot (forks row 1187, 2026-11-20). Every scripts/*.mjs that HAS a `selftest` mode is a member of exactly one suite, and a member is ONE FILE: suite/members/<organ>.json = { suite, argv, live } (suite: one of the three below; argv: what follows the organ's path — ["selftest"], or [] for an organ that is its own selftest, test_coach_v2; live: null, or the reason the hermetic profile names it LIVE and does not run it). When you add an organ with a selftest, create its member file in the same commit: a new file, never an edit to a line another unit edits (the && strings this replaced conflicted on every pair of units that each added a member — ci/mhot/MHOT_SPEC.md). scripts/organism_test.mjs `coverage` reads the files through its ONE reader (suiteRoll) and reds an organ with a selftest and no file (orphan), a file naming no organ (ghost), a file that does not parse or names no suite (defect) and two files for one organ (double-billing). `node scripts/organism_test.mjs roll` prints the roll. The prose this replaced — the 4 Aug measurements, the eleven organs added then, and the bare-invocation history of test_coach_v2 and claudegen — stands verbatim at 5759cce:package.json.
scripts._audit_suite_law: THE MEASUREMENT ORGANS (12 Aug 2026). The third suite. These are the organs that measure the organism itself — the sandbox and its canaries, the static IR, the runtime tracer, the mutant matrix, the token meter, the temporal/herd model, the front door, and (15 Aug 2026) archive_audit — the 2046 reader rehearsed early, which is here for the same cost reason: its selftest spawns two child processes to prove the independence guard bites from OUTSIDE the process it guards, and its `run` mode walks 34,000 records. They live in their own suite for ONE reason: COST. Several build a full git-ls-files sandbox and run for minutes, and folding them into squad:selftest would make the fast pre-commit glance slow enough that people stop running it. The coverage law in organism_test.mjs holds them to exactly the same standard as every other organ — a member file whose suite is audit:selftest is as covered as one naming either other suite (unit mhot, row 1187: the member files under suite/members are the single membership record; SUITE_NAMES names the three suites).
scripts._runner_law: AUDIT 6 Aug 2026 · re-shaped by unit mhot (forks row 1187). The three suite scripts above are FAST-FAIL chains: `node scripts/organism_test.mjs chain <suite>` runs that suite's member files (suite/members/*.json, in file-name order) and STOPS at the first red with its exit code — good for a pre-commit glance and the away-day lane, wrong as the net. Measured 6 Aug: brain.mjs sat at position 16 of 43 in the old organism:selftest && string, so one red organ left the 27 AFTER it unrun and unreported, and the suite said 'failed' rather than '27 unverified'. A net whose coverage silently SHRINKS when something breaks is the wrong shape. `npm test` is the authority: it reads the same member files (so they stay the single membership record) and runs every member INDEPENDENTLY, reporting all of them. Use the chain to fail fast; use `npm test` to know.
